cards.text: Paul (also called Saul) and Barnabas have been sent out by the Holy Spirit, with John along as their helper (Acts 13:2-5, 9). Now Paul and his companions set sail from Paphos and come to Perga in Pamphylia, where John leaves them. Why? The text doesn't say, friend, and I'm a cookie stamper, NOT a mind reader.

cards.question: John leaves Paul and his companions at Perga. Where does he go back to?

cards.text: From Perga, Paul and his companions travel inland to Pisidian Antioch. Then, on the Sabbath, they walk in somewhere and take a seat.

cards.question: On the Sabbath in Pisidian Antioch, where do Paul and his companions go in and sit down?
After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders send word to Paul and his companions, inviting them to speak. What do the leaders ask for?

answers.text: A word of encouragement for the people
A report from the church in Jerusalem
A reading from the scroll of Isaiah

cards.text: Paul stands up, motions with his hand, and begins to speak. Friend, I talk with my WHOLE mustache, so I respect a man who gets it done with ONE hand.

cards.question: Paul's first words in the synagogue call out two groups. Who are they?

answers.text: Men of Israel and Gentiles who fear God
Priests and Levites from the temple

cards.text: Then Paul starts WAY back. He says God chose Israel's fathers, made them a great people during their stay in Egypt, led them out of that land with an uplifted arm, and endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.

cards.question: Paul says God vanquished seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to His people as an inheritance.

cards.text: Paul says all this took about 450 years, and after that God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet. Then the people asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled forty years, and NO, friend, not the Saul who's also called Paul (Acts 13:9).

cards.question: After removing Saul, God raises up a new king and testifies that he is "a man after My own heart" who will carry out His will. Who is this king?

cards.text: Paul says that from David's descendants, God has brought Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised. Before Jesus arrived, John the Baptist (Matthew 3:1), not the John who left at Perga, preached a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

cards.question: As John is completing his course, he says there's One coming after him whose sandals he isn't worthy to untie. John is saying he himself is that One.

cards.text: Then Paul says it's to US that this message of salvation has been sent. He says the people of Jerusalem and their rulers didn't recognize Jesus, and in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.

cards.question: Paul says the people of Jerusalem and their rulers found solid ground for a death sentence against Jesus.

cards.text: Even with no ground, they asked Pilate, the governor (Matthew 27:2), to have Him executed. When they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.

cards.question: Paul says that after God raised Jesus from the dead, He was seen for many days by those who had traveled with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Now they are His ___ to the people.

cards.text: And now Paul brings the good news this whole sermon has been baking toward: what God promised their fathers, He has fulfilled for their children by raising up Jesus. As it's written in the second Psalm: "You are My Son; today I have become Your Father."

Paul says God raised Him from the dead, never to see decay, and he quotes Isaiah 55:3 about the holy and sure blessings promised to David. Then he quotes Psalm 16:10: "You will not let Your Holy One see decay."

cards.question: Paul says David served God's purpose in his own generation and then fell asleep. What happened to David's body?

answers.text: It was buried and saw decay
It was taken up to heaven
It was never buried at all

cards.text: But the One God raised from the dead did not see decay. So Paul lets them know that through Jesus, the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to them.

cards.question: Paul says that through Jesus, everyone who ___ is justified from everything the law of Moses could not justify them from.

cards.text: Paul doesn't wrap up with a polite little thank-you, friend. He warns them to watch out that what was spoken by the prophets doesn't happen to them, and he quotes Habakkuk 1:5, words to scoffers about a work being done in their days.

cards.question: The words Paul quotes say the scoffers would believe this work right away if someone told them about it.

cards.text: The sermon's done, and Paul and Barnabas head for the door. But the people in that synagogue are not done with them.

cards.question: As Paul and Barnabas leave the synagogue, what do the people urge them to do?

answers.text: Write the message on a scroll

cards.text: After the synagogue is dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism follow Paul and Barnabas. These two have followers, and NOT the phone kind.

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas urge the people following them to continue in the ___ of God.

cards.text: On the following Sabbath, nearly the WHOLE city gathers to hear the word of the Lord. Friend, the biggest crowd I ever pulled was the family whose kitchen I lived in, crowding the counter to steal dough, and they were NOT there for me.

cards.question: But when the Jews see the crowds, they are filled with ___.

cards.text: And they blasphemously contradict what Paul is saying.

cards.question: When they're contradicted, Paul and Barnabas back down and give a quiet, careful answer.

cards.text: Paul and Barnabas tell them it was necessary to speak the word of God to them first. But since they reject it and don't consider themselves worthy of eternal life, Paul and Barnabas are about to make a turn, and friend, I mean a HARD turn.

cards.question: Since the word is rejected, who do Paul and Barnabas say they will turn to now?
Paul and Barnabas say this is what the Lord has commanded them, quoting Isaiah 49:6: "I have made you a light for the Gentiles…" What is that light meant to bring to the ends of the earth?

cards.text: When the Gentiles hear this, they rejoice and glorify the word of the Lord. And all who were appointed for eternal life believe.

cards.question: After all this, the word of the Lord stays inside the synagogue walls.

cards.text: But the Jews incite the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. Then they stir up persecution against Paul and Barnabas.

cards.question: What does the persecution in Pisidian Antioch do to Paul and Barnabas?

answers.text: Drives them out of the district
Puts them in the city jail

cards.question: Driven out of the district, Paul and Barnabas shake the ___ off their feet in protest against them.

cards.text: Then Paul and Barnabas head on to Iconium.

cards.question: At the end of all this, the disciples are filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

cards.text: Keep that apron on, friend. This journey is NOT over, and I'm not telling you one crumb more than that.
